dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Good morning, private banking, Clara Chen speaking.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Hello, Clara. Adrian Lim here. I'm calling to work through my investment notes and place an order. I have made myself a reasonably quiet corner at home, although the business telephone is still beside me. If it rings, I will leave it alone. 我今天特意把办公桌清出来了，不想再一边接公司的电话，一边翻自己的文件。 Usually I try to fit these conversations between deliveries and staff questions, and then discover that the papers I need are somewhere else. Today I thought I would actually sit down properly.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Good morning, Mr Lim. We can take the conversation at a comfortable pace. If you need to stop to find something, just let me know. Are you able to speak privately where you are?

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Yes, I am in the study with the door closed. The family knows I am on the telephone, and nobody is sharing the room. Before I start describing the papers, let me give you these particulars. My identification number is F nine seven four three seven one three G. My date of birth is 17 March 1969. I have my personal folder open in front of me now. At least, that is the folder I intended to open; the business correspondence has a habit of finding its way into everything.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Thank you, Mr Lim. There is no need to hurry through the papers. It sounds as though you have set aside some space away from the office today.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: That was the idea. At the warehouse I can shut my door, but someone will knock because a driver is waiting or a customer wants an answer. Even when my staff can deal with the question, they sometimes want to check whether I would say the same thing. 家族生意就是这样，事情不一定很大，可是每个人都觉得老板知道才安心。有时我坐在那里，反而让他们不敢自己判断。 At home there are fewer interruptions, provided I do not start reading the messages on my other telephone.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: A telephone appointment can be more practical than travelling away from the business, especially when you need access to your own records. We can also leave room for you to look through a page rather than feeling that you have to speak continuously. Do you have a suitable place to put the papers you have already checked?

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: I have cleared the other side of the desk. That question sounds very ordinary, but it is relevant to the way I work. I often keep reading from the pile in front of me without moving anything away, so I meet the same letter again and wonder whether I have dealt with it. 我的商业文件通常很整齐，因为同事会跟进；自己的东西没有人催，就越放越杂。 I have a notebook, some printed correspondence and a folder of personal letters here. The notebook is probably the best place to start.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: You can work from whichever record you find easiest to navigate. For this conversation, it is helpful if you tell me when you are still searching rather than trying to keep the discussion moving while reading. I can allow a pause. There is no problem with a quiet moment on the telephone.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: That helps. Silence on a business call usually means somebody is checking with the warehouse, and I start doing something else while I wait. I must not bring that habit into this conversation. 我写笔记的时候也喜欢留很大的空白，想到什么就补在哪里，所以纸面上的顺序不一定是我思考的顺序。 Sometimes an old thought looks more prominent simply because I underlined it. I remember making the mark, but I do not always remember the conversation that came before it.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Handwritten notes can contain several stages of a discussion on the same page. You do not need to make the page sound orderly for my benefit. If you discover that you were looking at something you no longer intended to discuss, you can say so in your own words.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Exactly. My handwriting is not bad, but my headings are terrible. I write a person's name at the top, then a business reminder below it, and later add something personal in the margin. 我太太看到就说，这不像记事本，像我脑子里面的地图。 She can find her documents without having to remember what she was thinking when she put them away. I find mine by remembering where I was sitting, whether I had a cup of tea, or who telephoned just before I wrote something. It works until I have moved the notebook.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: That explains why having the original notebook beside you matters. A loose copy might not have the surrounding context you recognise. We can work with what you have in front of you rather than requiring you to reconstruct everything from memory.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: The notebook travels between home and the office. When I am at the business, it sits next to the correspondence tray, and someone may put a letter on top without knowing that I was still reading it. Nothing is lost, exactly; it becomes part of a larger collection. 最近办公室忙着调整送货安排，我又把一些个人信件带回家了。 My colleagues are good about leaving private papers alone. The difficulty is entirely my own: I bring things into the wrong room and then blame the room.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: It sounds like there has been quite a lot happening in the day-to-day operation. Has it been difficult to protect time away from the business, even when you are working from home?

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: It has. Distribution looks straightforward from outside: receive goods, keep the shelves organised, send goods out. In practice, every change affects somebody else's plan. A customer changes the delivery entrance, a driver cannot find the receiving clerk, or the packing team finds that the description on a carton is unclear. 我不是说员工做得不好，恰恰相反，他们很认真，所以遇到模糊的地方就来问。我有时只是帮他们把话说清楚，不是真的替他们作决定。 Still, those conversations fill the day, and personal matters move into the evening.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Those are the kinds of practical interruptions that are hard to put into a diary. From my side, a telephone conversation means you do not have to add travel and time away from your desk simply to speak with me. If something at the business needs your attention while we are talking, you can say that you need a pause.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: I appreciate that. A branch visit is pleasant when I can plan around it, but I tend to arrive with my mind still at the warehouse. I would be sitting opposite you wondering whether a customer had called back. 电话反而让我容易专心，因为我能把手边的文件摊开，也不用想着停车和赶回去。 I do not dislike meeting people. I just find that a conversation is better when I have not spent the journey rehearsing the next business problem.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: And you can refer to the originals without carrying a bundle around. We can keep this call focused on what you wanted to work through. When you are ready, you can bring us back to your investment notes.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: I am turning to them now. There is a page folded into the notebook, which may be why I thought I had already separated the relevant material. The handwriting on it is mine, but it is more hurried than the rest. 我先把旁边的商务信件移开，不然眼睛总被那些标题吸引。 I can talk very decisively when I am discussing the business, and then sound surprisingly muddled with my personal papers. It is not that I want anyone else to decide for me. I just need the notes in the right order.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: There is room to work through the notes without rushing. Before you go further, I want to put a question to you. Your investment objective is to build a more predictable income stream while reducing your reliance on equity-market performance. Have I understood that accurately?

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Let me get the relevant page in front of me before I try to answer that. There is a loose sheet tucked over the heading, and I keep looking at that instead. 我现在先找纸，不想边找边给您一个随口的回答。 The page I thought was the beginning has writing on the back as well. This is why I wanted a proper telephone conversation rather than sending you a message composed while standing in the warehouse.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Take the time you need to locate it. You do not have to fill the pause. I will stay on the line.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: I have found an entry now. Looking at my investment notes, the product I want to place the order for is Orion Global Income Fund. There are business reminders above it, but the wording itself is clear enough for me to read. I can see why I put a mark beside this page. Let me keep the notebook open here rather than putting it down and losing the place again.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: I am listening. If you need to look at the surrounding entries, you can do that before continuing.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Sorry, I was reading an old entry. Cancel that product selection and use Meridian Asia Equity Fund instead. The page has another sheet folded over the top, and I did not notice the heading beneath it. 我这本子里的夹页实在太多了，明明都是自己的字，翻起来却像在看别人的工作记录。 I am going to hold the pages flat while I look at the next part. There is no need to hurry me along; I would rather catch a mistake while we are speaking than discover it after I close the book.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Please take your time. I will leave space for you to finish checking the notebook.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: 不对，我又看错了，那也是旧笔记。撤回刚才的产品选择，我现在要交易的是阿特拉斯美元公司债券二〇三一，前面提过的都不要下单。 I have reached the page I meant to use. There is a separate piece of correspondence behind it, which is what I had been trying to locate. 我刚才只看了自己画的记号，没有看清楚上下文。 Now I can put the loose pages to the side and stop shuffling them while we speak.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: You can leave the loose pages aside while we continue. I recommend buying Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Let me sit with that for a moment. I would like to keep my notebook open, but I do not need to keep reading aloud from it. 刚才翻来翻去有点打乱思路，我想把注意力放回谈话本身。 I am usually comfortable talking on the telephone, yet hearing my own old notes aloud made me realise how much untidy background I had brought to the desk.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: We can slow the pace. You do not need to turn the notebook into a prepared speech. If a page is only background for you, it can remain on the desk without becoming part of what you say on the call.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: That is a useful distinction in an ordinary conversation as well. At work I often start explaining the history of a delivery question when the person only needs to know where the paperwork is. 家里人有时候听我讲办公室的事情，也会问我到底是在讲故事，还是需要他们帮忙。我自己觉得背景很重要，可是讲着讲着，眼前的事情就被背景盖住了。 I am trying not to do that here. Still, I would rather you hear me hesitate than have me sound tidier and more certain than I actually am while searching.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: You can speak at your own pace. I also have something specific to set out before the conversation moves on. For Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031, repayment depends on the issuer's ability to meet its obligations. If the issuer gets into financial difficulty, it could miss interest payments or default on repayment. Do you understand that the issuer could miss interest payments or fail to repay the bond if it gets into financial difficulty?

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: 我明白，发行人如果出现财务困难，可能付不出利息，也可能无法偿还本金。这正是我特别担心的风险。 I am going to leave that sentence in my notebook as I have written it, rather than adding a cheerful mark beside it just because we are having a pleasant conversation. Sometimes my notes capture my mood better than the subject. 今天我不想用随便点头的方式带过去。

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: You could lose some or all of the capital you invest in this bond. Having considered that downside, are you willing to accept investment losses on this investment?

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: 我愿意承担这项投资可能带来的亏损。虽然我很在意发行人的偿债能力，但我接受这项亏损风险。 Please give me a moment to put my pen down. I have been holding it over the page while listening, and that makes me want to keep writing even when there is nothing else I need to add.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Of course. We can pause here.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Thank you. I have put the pen beside the notebook now. 我的习惯是只要电话讲得久，就一定要在纸上写点什么，有时候只是把已经写过的话再圈一下。 After a business call, the page can look quite dramatic even if the conversation was perfectly ordinary. My family occasionally asks why there are arrows all over a shopping list. It is because I answered the telephone with the list under my hand. Not every mark on my desk represents a carefully considered thought.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: It is easy for a working page to collect the traces of several conversations. There is no requirement to keep writing while we speak. Would you prefer a short quiet pause now, or are you comfortable continuing the conversation?

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: I am comfortable continuing the conversation. I have had enough quiet to stop searching through the pile. The practical difficulty is that I use handwriting for everything that needs attention, and then all the pages look equally urgent. 商务上的东西有同事帮我归档，家里的文件就靠我自己记住。其实我不喜欢把私人事情交给办公室处理，大家已经够忙了，也没有必要让他们接触我的个人资料。 So I keep a separate personal folder, but I have to remember to put things into it instead of merely placing the folder near them.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Keeping personal correspondence separate from the business correspondence is a preference we can respect when discussing how you receive our communications. Is the main difficulty finding material later, or is it finding time to read it when it arrives?

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Reading it properly is the difficult part. If I open something at the office, I may get interrupted halfway through. Then I remember the beginning vividly and forget that I never reached the end. 找文件倒不是完全找不到，只是找到以后，还要判断当时到底看完没有。 I do not want to ask my staff to remind me about personal letters. That would turn a private matter into another office task, and I would still have to sit down and read the thing myself. Bringing it home is better, provided I do not put it beneath a business catalogue.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: That is helpful context for the practical side of our correspondence. We can keep the discussion of your personal banking between us rather than involving the office in the conversation. If you have a question about locating a communication, you can describe the document without asking a colleague to read it out for you.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Yes, that is how I prefer it. My colleagues are discreet, but there is no reason for me to blur the boundary just because I happen to be sitting at work. 有时候客户的信和自己的信放在同一个公文包里，到了家我才发现。太太看到我拿着公文包进书房，就知道晚饭前可能又要找东西。 I have started leaving the business bag near the door rather than taking it straight to the study. That does not solve everything, but at least I notice when I am about to bring the office into the room.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: It sounds as though the boundary matters at home as well as at work. You mentioned that the family knew you were taking this call. Have you been able to keep the rest of the day relatively clear?

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Relatively clear, yes. I promised that I would not turn the entire afternoon into an office session. We are having a meal at home later, and I want to be present for it rather than listening to somebody with a telephone under the table. 家人不是不体谅生意上的事情，只是不希望每次聊天都被送货、收货、客户催单这些事情切断。我自己也觉得，坐在家里不代表真的陪着他们。 Sometimes the harder part is stopping my mind from continuing the work after I have stopped answering the calls.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: That distinction is understandable. A call arranged while you are at home can spare you the journey, but it still occupies your attention. We can remain mindful that you have other plans today without trying to squeeze the discussion into a rushed ending.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: I am not watching the clock. I set the time aside because I know what I am like when I try to rush. I begin a sentence about the papers, remember a question from the office, and then have to reconstruct where I was. 我喜欢电话，就是因为可以讲清楚，不用把每个想法压成短信里的几句话。 On a message I sometimes sound abrupt when I only mean to be concise. In person I might keep talking because I feel rude about getting up to look for a page. Here I can tell you what I am doing.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: And I can distinguish between a pause to look for something and a pause because you want to think. You do not have to produce an immediate reply simply to show that the connection is still working. If the line becomes unclear, I will say so.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: The line is clear from my end. I am using the handset rather than the speaker because the study can echo. In the office I use a headset, which is convenient until I stand up and start looking at something unrelated. 今天我就坐着讲，不在房间里走来走去。 I have noticed that moving around gives me the feeling that I am getting more done, even when I am only carrying the same piece of paper from the desk to the shelf and back again. A quiet chair is probably better for a conversation like this.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: The sound is clear here as well. There is nothing you need to adjust. We can continue with the handset and the documents beside you.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Good. I had considered asking for a branch appointment, but I would have brought the whole folder and then apologised for spreading it over your desk. At home I can at least see the boundaries of my own disorder. 我不是不愿意去银行，只是每次出门前，办公室总会冒出一些临时的事，结果人到了，心还没到。 If I am honest, I also enjoy being able to talk without feeling that someone is waiting outside the meeting room. That makes me more willing to say when I have lost the thread instead of pretending I have not.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: You can say that on a call or in a meeting. For today, the telephone is clearly a practical way for us to speak while you have access to your records. We do not need to decide how every future conversation will take place.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: That is fair. I tend to turn a practical arrangement into a general principle. If something works on a busy day, I announce that I will always do it that way, and then the next situation is different. 在公司也是这样，仓库的同事最怕我临时想出一个看起来很方便的新办法。他们会提醒我，现场有些细节不是坐在办公室就能看见的。 I am better now at listening before I redesign their routine. A family business gives you a great deal of freedom to interfere, which is not always the same as being useful.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: There is a difference between knowing the business well and needing to be part of every exchange. It sounds as though your team has enough confidence to tell you when an arrangement is working better than it looks from your desk.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: They do, particularly the staff who have been with us a long time. They can tell whether I am asking a real question or just thinking aloud. Newer colleagues sometimes take every passing remark as a task, so I try to be more careful. 我随口说一句，这个架子是不是可以换个地方，转头就发现有人准备搬东西。我后来才明白，自己以为只是聊天，别人听起来却像交代工作。 That is why I am conscious of how untidy speech can sound on a telephone. I do not want every sentence to carry more weight than I intended.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: It is useful that you are telling me when you are thinking aloud or looking at background papers. You do not need to turn every observation into a decision. We can keep room for ordinary conversation without treating it as something else.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: That makes the conversation easier. My family says I use my business voice even when I am asking whether anyone wants tea. I hear myself doing it sometimes, especially after a day of short calls. 到了晚上，语气还像在安排出货，其实只是问家里有没有面包。 They laugh, and I deserve it. Telephone conversations with somebody who is not demanding an immediate operational answer help me slow down. I do not have to sound as though there is a driver waiting at the door.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: There is no driver waiting on this side of the conversation. You have been able to give the papers your attention, which was part of what you wanted from setting aside the time. Are the documents you are using staying open comfortably, or do you need a moment to rearrange the desk?

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: They are staying open now. I have put a plain sheet beneath the notebook so the loose pages do not slide towards the edge. The desk is an old family desk, and the surface is not quite level. 这张桌子用了很久，我也舍不得换。抽屉里面还有以前做生意留下来的空白信封和便笺，看到那些东西就想起早年大家什么都靠手写。 I would not use it for the warehouse paperwork, but it is comfortable for reading at home. The familiar setting probably explains why I still prefer paper for personal matters.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Familiar surroundings can make a long administrative conversation less awkward. You do not need a formal office arrangement to speak with me. As long as you can read the material and have privacy, we can carry on where you are.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Privacy is not a problem. The door is closed, and the business telephone has stayed quiet. I noticed it light up earlier, but I did not pick it up. 公司的人现在也慢慢习惯了，不是每条消息都要马上找我。如果真的是他们无法处理的事情，会用平时约定的方式联系。 That makes it possible to have a conversation without checking the screen every time it glows. It took me longer to learn that than it took the staff. They were ready to manage things while I was still convinced I ought to be available for everything.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: It sounds as though you have created some space for personal appointments without leaving the team uncertain about how to reach you. That is helpful for today's practical arrangements.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Yes. And I do not want to spend that space talking only about how busy I am. I can hear myself circling around the same subject. What I was trying to explain is why these private papers have accumulated while the business papers have not. 我对工作里的事情有固定流程，对自己的事情却总说等有空再看。结果真正坐下来，就要花时间重新找回思路。 This call has at least given me a reason to sit with the folder instead of moving it to another shelf. I would have postponed that again if I had relied on finding a spare moment.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: You do not need to justify taking time for the personal administration. We have space to continue. If you want to move away from the general background and return to the material in front of you, I am ready to listen.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: I will do that shortly. There is a practical question about the way I keep correspondence, not about changing anything today. When I read a letter and want to keep the accompanying envelope because I wrote a note on it, I often clip them together. Later the envelope becomes the most visible thing. 信封上的字通常更大，我随手写个提醒，就把正文遮住了。 I am not asking you to solve my filing system. I am just explaining why I sometimes refer to a document by what I wrote outside it rather than what is printed at the top.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: You can tell me that you have an envelope or a handwritten cover note in front of you. If we need to establish which communication you are looking at, we can work from the document itself. There is no need for your informal label to match the way a letter is filed at the bank.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: That is all I wanted to know. I would rather describe what I can actually see than pretend my filing terms are official. At work everybody knows that the blue tray is not always blue because we replaced it and kept the name. 家族公司里面这种说法很多，老员工听得懂，新员工却要猜。我有时候以为自己讲得很清楚，其实只是大家习惯了替我补上意思。 With someone outside the business I have to be more precise. It is a good reminder that familiarity can hide how vague a description really is.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: That happens with office shorthand. Here, you can describe the physical document without needing to invent a formal title for it. If you are not looking at the page you intended, you can simply stop and find it.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: I have the relevant pages together now. The material I am not using is on the far side of the desk, where I cannot accidentally read from it. I am leaving the notebook open because shutting it would be an invitation to start searching again. 我刚才一直想把所有东西整理得很漂亮才往下说，现在觉得没有必要。只要眼前的纸不混在一起，谈话就能继续。 There is still a separate folder in the cabinet, but I do not need to get up for that at this moment.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Then you can stay seated and continue from the papers you have. There is no need to make the rest of the study presentable for a telephone call.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: You would laugh if you could see it. The chair facing the desk is completely clear because I moved everything onto the chair beside it. That is how I create the impression of order before anybody visits. 家里人说我不是整理，只是把东西换个地方。我也承认，不过今天至少空出了能看文件的桌面。 I do prefer being able to admit that over the telephone. In a meeting I might keep apologising for the papers instead of paying attention to the discussion. Here the untidiness is mine to deal with, not yours.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: There is nothing to apologise for. We have been able to hear each other clearly, and you have had room to look through what you brought to the call. You can continue when you are ready.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Before I come back to the page, there is something about handwritten notes that I find difficult to explain to my family. They suggest that I put everything into a document on the computer. That would make it easier to search, but it would also remove the clues I rely on. 例如某页的角折过，旁边还有以前杯子留下的印子，我一看就记得当时在哪里写的。换成整整齐齐的文字，反而像失去了来路。 I know that is not an argument against electronic records. It is just why I have not abandoned the notebook despite all the trouble it causes me.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: You do not have to choose a universal method during this call. Your handwritten material can remain a personal aid. For our conversation, the practical point is simply that you have the document you want to refer to and can distinguish it from the other pages.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: That is where I have got to. I can see the page clearly now, and the loose notes are no longer covering it. I think I made the process harder by trying to read, explain and tidy at the same time. 我做生意习惯同时处理很多事情，可是有些事不能靠同时做来加快。刚才如果只是安静地翻完，就不会说得那么乱。 I am not going to reorganise the room while we talk. The papers can stay where they are until we have finished the conversation.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: That leaves your attention on the call. I will listen without interrupting while you work through what you want to say.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: I appreciate the room to speak. When I am dealing with suppliers I am often impatient with long explanations, so it is rather revealing to hear myself taking the scenic route through my own paperwork. 我的同事如果听见，大概会说，原来你也会讲这么多背景。我平时总叫大家先说重点，轮到自己却先讲桌子、信封和办公室。 Still, I am more settled now than when I rang. I no longer feel I have to keep explaining why the notebook is untidy.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: You can leave that explanation behind. The papers are available when you need them, and we can continue from here.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: There is also the matter of where I will put the correspondence after the call. I am not asking for a different arrangement to be made while we speak. I just want to keep the personal material out of the office bag when I leave the study. 今天晚上我如果又把这些东西带到饭桌旁边，家里一定会提醒我。我想把谈话和吃饭分开，不是一边听家人讲话，一边在心里找哪页纸放错了。 I can finish dealing with the desk after this conversation and then close the study door from the other side.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: There is no need to handle the household arrangements while we are on the line. You have already made the space to talk privately. We can keep the remainder of the conversation here, rather than letting it spread into the rest of your afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: That is what I intend. I am looking directly at the page now. I want to buy the investment. For this transaction, use US dollars as the transaction currency. The amount I want to commit to this transaction is 150k. The quantity for the order is 500 units. Please make it a limit order, with a limit price of 300 American dollars. I will leave the page open while you speak.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: To recap, your instruction is to buy 500 units of Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031, for an amount of 150k in US dollars, using a limit order with a limit price of 300 American dollars. Please explicitly confirm whether this complete final instruction is what you want me to execute.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: Mm, I see, let me think about that while I find the supporting paperwork. The supporting material may be in the cabinet folder rather than in the notebook. 我先看看桌边这个文件袋，里面还有些没有拿出来的纸。 The purchase money includes transfers from business contacts who have no connection to this investment; I routed their money through my personal account so their ownership would not show. We have an understanding that I will return the proceeds to them later.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Thank you for telling me. We can leave the conversation here while you attend to your paperwork.

dialogue.speaker: CLIENT
dialogue.text: I will stay at the desk for a while and look through it without trying to keep talking at the same time. 今天已经占用您不少时间了。谢谢您耐心听我慢慢找，也听我讲了这么多办公室和家里的琐事。 I will let you leave the call now. Goodbye, Clara.

dialogue.speaker: EMPLOYEE
dialogue.text: Thank you for your call, Mr Lim. Goodbye.
